Chapter 7: The Cost and Courage of Discipleship.
There’s always that moment on a journey when you realize just what it’s going to cost. If you’ve ever felt drawn to the upside-down kingdom, you’ll know it’s a road paved with both beauty and sacrifice. And the teacher? He never sugarcoats it. He says it straight: If you want to follow me, take up your cross.
That call—it’s echoed through history, challenging each new generation to pause, to really count the cost.
Sometimes, the price is obvious. Maybe it’s losing a job because you chose honesty over comfort. Or watching a friendship stretch thin, just because your priorities shifted. There’s that moment your reputation gets questioned, all because you dared to stand with someone the world would rather ignore.
But often, the sacrifices aren’t loud. They’re quiet, almost invisible. Letting go of an old grudge. Choosing forgiveness instead of getting even. Or saying goodbye to your own comfort just to help someone who really needs it.
Picture this: a man, well-respected by everyone around him, suddenly faces a choice. He’s always done what was expected, stayed right in line. But now, he’s being asked to risk his good name for someone everyone else avoids. He hesitates—who wouldn’t? The fear of losing what he’s built is real.
Still, when he finally steps forward, something shifts. He discovers a kind of freedom he’s never felt before—a sense of integrity that no one else can touch.
Or think of a young woman who’s tired of being invisible. In the upside-down kingdom, she finally finds her voice. She stands up for justice, even when it means facing criticism.
Here’s the thing: courage doesn’t arrive all at once. It grows, little by little, with every small step of faithfulness—every moment she chooses to believe that love really is stronger than fear.
Even the teacher’s journey is marked by pain. He’s misunderstood, rejected, and in the end, betrayed by those closest to him. But he doesn’t back down. Not once. Even when violence comes, he chooses forgiveness. That example? It becomes a lifeline for anyone who wants to follow in his steps.
Discipleship in the upside-down kingdom isn’t about getting everything right. It’s about showing up, again and again, even when the path is tough. It’s believing that every sacrifice made for love, for justice, is never wasted.
Most of us want our lives to mean something. But let’s be honest—not everyone’s willing to pay the price. The upside-down kingdom? It asks for everything. But here’s the surprise: it gives back so much more.
Sure, the cost is real. But so is the reward—a life filled with courage, with purpose, and that deep-down satisfaction of knowing you’re part of something so much bigger than yourself.
